newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi sees 97 public deficit at 3.3 pct - interview.
newsitem.headline: Prodi sees 97 public deficit at 3.3 pct - interview.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister was quoted as saying on Friday that Italy would not be able to bring down its budget deficit in 1997 to the three percent level required by the Maastricht treaty on monetary union.
"In all honesty we will get to 3.3 percent, rather than an exact three percent, meaning we will be in the range," Prodi told the International Herald Tribune (IHT) in an interview.
"And then we will examine with out European colleagues what we need to do," Prodi told the IHT.
But he added that in order to meet the three percent Maastricht goal he was prepared "to take extraordinary and supplementary steps if that is deemed necessary."
To avoid having to introduce a supplementary budget in the spring Italy would need a growth rate of two percent in 1997, the IHT quoted Prodi as saying.
The government's 62.5 trillion lire 1997 budget is currently making its way through parliament.

The lira was readmitted to the European Union's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at the weekend in what the government sees as an essential step towards joining Euriopean economic and monetary uinion (EMU) by 1999.
Prodi reaffirmed that he was prepared to resign if Italy failed to join EMU by the planned starting date.

"When I came to government there was no chance of attaining the Maastricht conditions. Now there is a high chance, let us say an increasing chance, and objective observers say there is a better than 50-50 chance of Italy's joining the first wave of countries launching the single currency," he added.
"Failure to make the 1999 EMU target date "would be an enormous tragedy," Prodi said.
